newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB REPORT - AUSTRALIAN WHEAT DRIVEN BY WEATHER.
newsitem.headline: AWB REPORT - AUSTRALIAN WHEAT DRIVEN BY WEATHER.

text.p: Australia's domestic wheat market continues to be driven by crop concerns in dry parts of the southern and eastern states, the Australian Wheat Board said on Friday.
The old crop domestic wheat market saw a relatively quiet week to Wednesday in anticipation of AWB tender results, it said in its weekly grain market report.
While most bids were submitted for new crop positions the tender saw a $15.00 increase in the reserve price as well as record tonnages tendered.
Market prices for old crop wheat rose correspondingly.
These factors were all the result of increasing concern about new crop prospects and the dry El Nino weather patterns over the rest of the growing season.

Rain of around 15 mm in south eastern parts of the grain belt later in the week had little impact on prices. However, an increase in rainfall would see a weakening in prices, AWB said. In the domestic feedgrain market sorghum prices rallied considerably because of weather concerns and as old crop barley prices in southern Australia continued to rise on stong demand. Unusually, these prices were higher than feed wheat and were supported by dairy demand in Victoria.
